### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**4** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8eef9a8db402b6d46b15cc2375f8acddbb0d7b7e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `becfa4ac2a42ebe7ad961235cd40ebe1ca8c318f` — the merge of head `3adedc914cebee085f7774754c3182a39d38dc34` into base `8eef9a8db402b6d46b15cc2375f8acddbb0d7b7e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin becfa4ac2a42ebe7ad961235cd40ebe1ca8c318f && git checkout becfa4ac2a42ebe7ad961235cd40ebe1ca8c318f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8eef9a8db402b6d46b15cc2375f8acddbb0d7b7e 3adedc914cebee085f7774754c3182a39d38dc34 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8eef9a8db402b6d46b15cc2375f8acddbb0d7b7e && git merge --no-ff 3adedc914cebee085f7774754c3182a39d38dc34

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8eef9a8db402b6d46b15cc2375f8acddbb0d7b7e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9634b5a3388d2fdd5229e0643a63da21543c7040`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/lint/src/validate-list-view-field-refs.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-list-view-field-refs.test.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/lint/src/index.ts, .changeset/26719-list-view-chart-foreign-dataset.md, content/docs/data-modeling/analytics.mdx + packages/lint/src/reference-integrity-suite.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/runtime-authoring-gate.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-gate.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/dataset.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts, ui/packages/plugin-charts/src/ObjectChart.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/objectViewListRenderer.tsx, examples/app-showcase/src/ui/views/task.view.ts, examples/app-showcase/src/ui/views/project.view.ts, examples/app-showcase/src/ui/datasets/chart-gallery.dataset.ts

Read-only review of card #26719 (body, triage 6446947560, claim 6448354345, os-dev-report 6450182672, claim amendment 6450303047), PR #26842 (body, file list, net diff of the six files against `main` at the merge base 0ea90c7a), and the check-runs on the head. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set changes the diff implies, each judged:

1. **One new refusal, `list-view-chart-dataset-foreign-object` (`error`), fired once per list view at `chart.dataset` when the view's resolved bound object differs from the `object` of the declared dataset its `chart.dataset` names.** Right. `checkChartDataset` reads `datasetObjects` built from `recordsOf(stack.datasets)` and compares object names only; the message names the dataset and both objects, `where` names the view, the hint is one line with no tracker number (`check:doc-authoring` is green).
2. **Width against the card's defect.** The card's symptom is "nothing checks that the dataset belongs to the view's object"; the triage ruling (6446947560) states the refusal as "a dataset whose object is not the view's object", and the claim and its amendment repeat that. The diff refuses exactly that set and nothing more: it runs only when the binding resolves (`graph.has(object)`), only when the dataset resolves and declares an `object`, and never on a draft (`evaluateRuntimeAuthoringGate` returns before any rule when `state !== 'active'`). Right, and no wider.
3. **The include-reachable case is refused on purpose.** Judged against the cited code and accepted. `DatasetSchema.object` is the FROM ("Base object — the FROM"), and `include` lists to-one relationships from that base object whose joins are compiled by the engine (packages/spec/src/ui/dataset.zod.ts lines 584 to 595); a dataset over B that includes A still produces B's rows, grouped by A's columns. On the render side `objectViewListRenderer.tsx` hands `ObjectChart` only `dataset`, `dimensions`, `values` and `chartType`, and `ObjectChart.tsx` calls `queryDataset(schema.dataset, { dimensions, measures, runtimeFilter? })` with no list object and no list filter, so nothing scopes a foreign dataset to the list's records. Equality of the two object names is the one test that says the chart plots what the list lists; the dev's reasoning holds, and the test pins it both ways (`duly_task_by_owner` refused under the person list, admitted under the task list).
4. **Not judged: an unknown dataset, a dataset without `object`, an unresolved binding, the dataset's own package.** Right. Each has an owner (`chart-dataset-unknown`, the parse, `list-view-object-outside-closure` / `list-view-object-unknown` / skip 1), and a same-object dataset's object is inside the written package's closure by construction. The unknown-dataset gap at the view door is #26847, not this PR.
5. **The rule fires at the view publish door and at object writes, with the snapshot those doors carry.** Right. `validateListViewFieldRefs` is registered with `runtimeTypes: ['flow', 'view', 'object']` (reference-integrity-suite.ts line 337); `protocol-authoring-gate.ts` gathers `datasets` through `listCollection('dataset', 'datasets')` for every gated write (line 335 to 345) and hands them to `evaluateRuntimeAuthoringGate`, which folds the batch's pending datasets in (`runtime-authoring-gate.ts` line 1156) and passes `context.datasets` to `runRuntimeAuthoringRules`, whose `CONTEXT_STACK_KEYS` carries `datasets`. Only `objects` is narrowed to the package closure; the rule compares names, so the narrowing cannot hide a foreign dataset. `checkListView` walks all five shapes (`objects[].listViews`, `views[].list`, `views[].listViews`, the flattened overlay, the ViewItem `config`), with a list view's own `data.object` winning over its container's, and the check is placed after `graph.has(object)` and before `graph.get(object)` so an external object with no field map is still judged. The runtime-door test runs `runRuntimeAuthoringRules` at `type: 'view'` under a package closure with the datasets in context and asserts both the refusal and its control.
6. **Shipped corpus.** Zero findings. `examples/**` carries two chart list views: `task.view.ts` binds `showcase_task_metrics` (over `showcase_task`) under the task list, `project.view.ts` binds `showcase_project_metrics` (over `showcase_project`) under the project list. `packages/platform-objects` declares no chart list view (its charts are dashboard widgets). `Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus` and `Dogfood Regression Gate` are green on the head.
7. **Tests are non-vacuous.** The `[#26719]` block asserts the rule id and the exact path on every shape, the `where`, the three names in the message, the one-line hint under 200 characters, the silence of the three not-judged cases, the external-object case, `validate` and `build` failing, the runtime door refusing and admitting, and the `os explain` entry. Five controls sit beside eleven refusals; the dev's ablation of the single `checkChartDataset(...)` call reports 11 red and 5 green, which matches the block's shape. The block counts 16 cases as the body says.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/26719-list-view-chart-foreign-dataset.md`: `'@objectstack/lint': minor`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, a BREAKING banner, and one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. The PR body carries the same two declaration lines at line start. `narrowed` on a moved package takes at least `minor`: correct. The disposition is right: no schema key is added, removed, renamed or re-shaped, and only the author can say which of the three remedies applies, so no rewrite is prescribable; after 9634b5a3 the body carries the remedy and no FROM/TO block, which is what that disposition requires (`Check Changeset` green).
- An error-level narrowing that no conversion carries ships in 18.x as its own BREAKING minor under the amended standing ruling 「甲」 (record 6303865025), as the sibling list-view narrowings did; the card's triage ruled a located refusal at save. Consistent.
- `@objectstack/spec` is owed nothing. The diff touches no spec file, the rule lives in `packages/lint` where the list-view lint family lives, no spec surface registers lint rule ids (the sibling `list-view-group-order-unorderable` appears in `view.zod.ts` only inside a doc comment), and the `chart.dataset` description ("Dataset name to bind (ADR-0021)") makes no promise this refusal contradicts. The runtime door takes the rule through its dependency on `@objectstack/lint`, so one changeset is the right count.
- `CHANGELOG.md`, `content/docs/references/` and `content/docs/releases/` are untouched. The hand-written docs line in `content/docs/data-modeling/analytics.mdx` states the rule and the remedy.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Landing site.** The claim named `packages/spec`; the amendment 6450303047 corrected it to `packages/lint` (`validateListViewFieldRefs`) and states this corrects the claim, not the dev's scope. The diff is entirely inside that corrected surface plus its tests, docs and one changeset. Answered.
- **Security question from the claim.** The dev measured on the branch's base that the dataset read enforces the caller's object-level and row-level read on the foreign object (403 and 0-of-3 rows for a member); the amendment accepted it as no finding. Not re-measured here (read-only); recorded as the dev's measurement, accepted by the seat.
- **Out-of-scope finding (class a).** The view door never runs `validateChartBindings`, so an unknown dataset or a ghost measure still publishes 200. Filed as #26847 by the seat; the PR body names it as out of scope and the rule explanation defers `chart-dataset-unknown` to its owner. Escalated correctly, nothing left open.
- **`open_questions`.** The report lists none.
- **Branch name.** `claude/project-thread-xqvx1a` instead of an issue-slug branch; the claim records why (the platform assigns the thread's branch). `Implemented-by` below uses the measured branch.
- **Serial constraint with #26711.** This PR does not touch `view.zod.ts`; the branch merged `main` at 3ccc765c. Clear.
- **Check-runs on 9634b5a3, read at 2026-10-27T18:32Z.** Green: Lint & Repo Gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · CI release & engine gates, Lint · scoped (slot lookup & corpus, query-options erasure, tooling self-tests), Type Check · source gates, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Build & E2E UI, Test UI, Test Core 7/8, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected by code changes, Auto Label. Skipped by filter: Lint UI, Test UI shards, Temporal Conformance, Dogfood shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, 18.x upgrade harness, Packed-tarball smoke. Still in progress at that time: Type Check UI, Type Check · workspace, Test Core 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8 of 8. No check has failed. The landing waits for those to finish green; this record does not stand in for them.

**PR body against the diff.** One sentence is stale. Under "What changes", the line
"Changeset: `@objectstack/lint` minor, BREAKING accept-set narrowing, ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, FROM → TO and the one-line fix in the body."
describes the changeset as it stood before 9634b5a3; that commit removed the FROM → TO block because the ADR-0087 gate refuses a rewrite prescription under that disposition. Replacement:
"Changeset: `@objectstack/lint` minor, BREAKING accept-set narrowing, ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`; the body states the remedy and carries no FROM → TO rewrite, since that disposition refuses a prescription."
Every other sentence checked holds: the family choice over `validateChartBindings` (`runtimeTypes: ['flow', 'report']` at reference-integrity-suite.ts line 441), the five shapes walked, the draft-not-gated behaviour, the corpus census, the 16-case count, and the "no `skills/**` file teaches list-view chart bindings" claim (`skills/objectstack-ui/rules/list-views.md` mentions neither `chart` nor `dataset`).

**Should-fix (not blocking).** The runtime door is pinned at `type: 'view'` only; a sibling case at `type: 'object'` with a foreign chart under `objects[].listViews` would pin the object door's snapshot too. The suite row and the pure-function shape test cover it today, so this is a follow-up, not a condition of landing.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-xqvx1a`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzfhobWEgUUrjz4rrbh`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · `domain:spec` seat 1 (#6017) · session `session_01WGufzfhobWEgUUrjz4rrbh` · 2026-10-27T19:10Z

Head `3adedc914cebee085f7774754c3182a39d38dc34`. Card #26719 (triage `6446947560`), claim `6448354345` with amendment `6450303047` (the file surface is `packages/lint`, not `packages/spec`), dev report `6450182672`.

- **Contract review:** owed at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER because the PR is a narrowing. The full review (`6450478244`) at `9634b5a3` was a PASS with no must-fix. It judged that:
  - the refusal is exactly as wide as the triage ruling: the dataset's `object` must equal the list view's object;
  - the include-reachable case is refused on purpose and correctly, because `include` adds to-one columns and never a second row set, and the console hands `queryDataset` no list object or filter;
  - the rule fires at both the `view` and `object` doors with the snapshot they carry;
  - the shipped corpus has zero findings.
- **Should-fixes, both closed:**
  1. The stale changeset sentence in the PR body. The seat rewrote it.
  2. Nothing pinned the `object` door. `3adedc91` adds two runtime-door tests at `type: 'object'`: a foreign-dataset chart under `listViews` is refused at `listViews.by_status.chart.dataset`, and an own-object control passes clean. The dev's ablation (the `checkChartDataset` call removed) reds the refusal and leaves the control green.
- **Security:** the dataset read enforces object and row read on the foreign object, so there is no finding.
- **Out of scope:** the view door never runs `validateChartBindings`, so an unknown dataset or measure on a chart list view publishes `200`. Filed as #26847.
- **Shape:** `Fixes #26719`, 6 files, +323/−0. `@objectstack/lint` minor. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`. ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. `check-governed-merges --pr 26842`: NOT governed.
- **Gates:** check-runs on this head are 40 success, 7 skipped and 0 red. `mergeable_state` is clean.
- **Landing:** Tier S. `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` in this act.
